limitations: GPU interval covers synthetic scene shading and the selected reconstruction; readback is outside timing.
CPU interval covers command allocation, encoding, and commit; GPU waiting is excluded.
Native shades four times as many pixels as every low-resolution route. These timings do not prove game speedup.
Temporal uses a static plane, depth=0.5, zero non-jitter motion, matched Halton jitter, and persistent history.
Temporal output error includes jitter phase and filter history; no moving geometry or disocclusion is exercised.
Nearest is a compute resample because Metal blit does not resize textures.
No process names, local paths, device names, registry IDs, or personal identifiers are collected.
API validation changes timing overhead; use a separate validation-disabled run for performance conclusions.
Game Mode activation, guest rendering, presentation, frame pacing, and thermal steady state are outside this experiment.
